# Field

A label, control, hint and error laid out together, the same way every time.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Accessible first</span></p>

## When to use it

**In Accessible first:** Label, hint and error in the same place on every question.

- **Use it when:** Every form control that needs a label, a hint or an error.
- **Not when:** A control that is not part of a form, such as a search box in a toolbar.

Instead:

- [Label](./label.md): The label on its own.

## How Accessible first uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Field label or column header</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> type.label, above the field, always visible</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A placeholder as the label</div></div><div class="cap">Labels must stay visible while typing.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">An error message</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> color.status.danger, an icon and a sentence next to the field</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Color alone</div></div><div class="cap">People must know what went wrong and where.</div></div></div>

## Why it works this way

Field looks the way it does because of 4 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Field, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-tasks-q1"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is the main task?</b><code>tasks.q1</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Complete a form</div><p>People must finish the form.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Field</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>vertical</b>: Every question: the label above the field, always visible.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Input group: inline-start</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Field decision would reopen</small><p>and 6 answers that follow from it: <b>Completion without errors</b>, <b>A task that fails</b>, <b>One sitting</b>, and 3 more.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-human-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How do people recall the interface?</b><code>human.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">They see it fresh each time</div><p>Nobody remembers the interface from last time.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Field</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>responsive</b>: One layout on every device, so people meet the same form every time.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: secondary</code> <code>Button: ghost</code> <code>Button: disabled</code> <code>Toggle: default</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Field decision would reopen</small><p>and 1 answer that follow from it: <b>Actions and status</b>.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
- One idea per sentence. Put the action first.
- Never blame the person.
- Use: Continue, Change, Start, You. Avoid: Invalid, Utilise, Submit, Error code.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Continue
- `content.action.cancel`: Go back
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Start a new application

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The label, hint and error are linked to the control, so they are read with it. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add field
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.
